If completion or contract linkage is unresolved, answer unknown. With no established entire contract, a known final date remains informational and requires review.

sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. Series09 permits a calculated completion +120 raw baseline only for an explicitly identified entire contract and actual qualifying completion, after existing holds. Unresolved grouping/completion retains review: first +120 is a conservative checkpoint and known final +120 informational; passing the checkpoint alone does not establish expiry. Notice/account clocks, source windows, raw calendar and pending approval remain unchanged. Details and limits remain in the bound note.

October 13 complete Chapter 447 read and the General Court online compilation statement supersede the original access limitation. The website states currency through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026, but identifies Thomson Reuters bound volumes/supplements as the official version. Specific procedure, interpretation and appointment limits remain.
Additional service, recording and amount conditions described below remain mandatory; this calculator is not a notice-sending or lien-filing service.

This is court attachment, not recorder filing. Start well before the target; RSA 511-A procedure remains unread. The October 13 reads include Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), describing an indivisible lien under one entire contract and whole-lien preservation within its historical 90-day period; McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005, describes the 120-day completion clock but decides priority; Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), rejects completed-contract replacement and receivership extensions. The retained first-delivery +120 date is a conservative review target, not a universal statutory expiration. Contract identity/completion, CAP reporter accuracy and current treatment remain qualified.

After the applicable owner notice, provide written accounts as often as once in thirty days. Late notice protects sums then due or that may thereafter become due to the contractor, agent or subcontractor. Unknown mortgage/posting facts require review; do not omit lender notice.

The General Court website states currency through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026. Its displayed LSA links stop at 2023; no separate 2025–2026 bill/LSA search or bound official-edition review is recorded here. Retain the existing targeted election/Thanksgiving evidence and attachment-procedure limits.

preliminary_notice.name: Owner and construction lender notices
preliminary_notice.description: Lender notice is required within fifteen business days of the later trigger. Remote suppliers also notify owner BEFORE first delivery; retain both candidates.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: For an established entire contract with actual qualifying furnishing completed, secure the lien by court attachment within the calculated 120-day baseline. This is not a determination of notice coverage, amount, priority or attachment procedure; start court work well before this date.

questions.label: Does this lien claim concern one identified entire contract rather than distinct separate orders?
questions.help: Confirm the contract governing the qualifying materials in this claim. One jobsite, customer, account or group of invoices does not establish one entire contract. If grouping is unresolved, answer unknown. A later replacement, invoice, payment, materials not supplied by you or receivership does not restart a completed contract.

questions.label: Have you actually completed qualifying furnishing for this claim?
questions.help: If this claim is under one identified entire contract, confirm actual qualifying completion of your furnishing under that contract and enter that date. Do not use a planned delivery, project-wide latest delivery, payment, later invoice alone, corrective/trivial replacement or another supplier’s materials to restart a completed contract. If completion or contract linkage is unresolved, answer unknown. With no established entire contract, a known final date remains informational and requires review.

sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. Series09 permits a calculated completion +120 raw baseline only for an explicitly identified entire contract and actual qualifying completion, after existing holds. Unresolved grouping/completion retains review: first +120 is a conservative checkpoint and known final +120 informational; passing the checkpoint alone does not establish expiry. Notice/account clocks, source windows, raw calendar and pending approval remain unchanged. Details and limits remain in the bound note.

October 13 complete Chapter 447 read and the General Court online compilation statement supersede the original access limitation. The website states currency through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026, but identifies Thomson Reuters bound volumes/supplements as the official version. Specific procedure, interpretation and appointment limits remain.
Additional service, recording and amount conditions described below remain mandatory; this calculator is not a notice-sending or lien-filing service.

This is court attachment, not recorder filing. Start well before the target; RSA 511-A procedure remains unread. The October 13 reads include Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), describing an indivisible lien under one entire contract and whole-lien preservation within its historical 90-day period; McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005, describes the 120-day completion clock but decides priority; Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), rejects completed-contract replacement and receivership extensions. The retained first-delivery +120 date is a conservative review target, not a universal statutory expiration. Contract identity/completion, CAP reporter accuracy and current treatment remain qualified.

After the applicable owner notice, provide written accounts as often as once in thirty days. Late notice protects sums then due or that may thereafter become due to the contractor, agent or subcontractor. Unknown mortgage/posting facts require review; do not omit lender notice.

The General Court website states currency through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026. Its displayed LSA links stop at 2023; no separate 2025–2026 bill/LSA search or bound official-edition review is recorded here. Retain the existing targeted election/Thanksgiving evidence and attachment-procedure limits.

recurring_notice_intake.label: Actual owner notice and written accounts
recurring_notice_intake.help: Enter actual written accounts and establish the separate actual owner notice. The latest actual act plus thirty days is an advisory checkpoint only; later accounts do not establish timely earlier coverage or a legal cadence reset.

preliminary_notice.name: Owner and construction lender notices
preliminary_notice.description: Lender notice is required within fifteen business days of the later trigger. Remote suppliers also notify owner BEFORE first delivery; retain both candidates.

notice_duties.name: Owner notice before furnishing
notice_duties.description: Give written notice to the owner or person having charge of the property before first furnishing. A later notice has the unpaid-balance limitations in RSA 447:6; preserve the existing late-notice and balance review path.

notice_duties.name: Construction lender notice
notice_duties.description: Provide written notice to the institution providing the construction funds within fifteen business days of the later of first furnishing or the actual jobsite lender posting. Include the name and address of the jobsite. Failure to provide this notice alone does not invalidate the lien (RSA 447:12-b(II)); preserve the bound service and business-day rules.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: For an established entire contract with actual qualifying furnishing completed, secure the lien by court attachment within the calculated 120-day baseline. This is not a determination of notice coverage, amount, priority or attachment procedure; start court work well before this date.

Conservative action date shown; the statutory deadline remains unresolved. Obtain qualified review before this date.

sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. Series09 permits a calculated completion +120 raw baseline only for an explicitly identified entire contract and actual qualifying completion, after existing holds. Unresolved grouping/completion retains review: first +120 is a conservative checkpoint and known final +120 informational; passing the checkpoint alone does not establish expiry. Notice/account clocks, source windows, raw calendar and pending approval remain unchanged. Details and limits remain in the bound note.

October 13 complete Chapter 447 read and the General Court online compilation statement supersede the original access limitation. This is court attachment, not recorder filing. Start well before the target; RSA 511-A procedure remains unread. The October 13 reads include Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), describing an indivisible lien under one entire contract and whole-lien preservation within its historical 90-day period; McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005, describes the 120-day completion clock but decides priority; Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), rejects completed-contract replacement and receivership extensions. The retained first-delivery +120 date is a conservative review target, not a universal statutory expiration. Contract identity/completion, CAP reporter accuracy and current treatment remain qualified.

After the applicable owner notice, provide written accounts as often as once in thirty days. Late notice protects sums then due or that may thereafter become due to the contractor, agent or subcontractor. Unknown mortgage/posting facts require review; do not omit lender notice.

The General Court website states currency through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026. Its displayed LSA links stop at 2023; no separate 2025–2026 bill/LSA search or bound official-edition review is recorded here. Retain the existing targeted election/Thanksgiving evidence and attachment-procedure limits.

recurring_notice_intake.label: Actual owner notice and written accounts
recurring_notice_intake.help: Enter actual written accounts and establish the separate actual owner notice. The latest actual act plus thirty days is an advisory checkpoint only; later accounts do not establish timely earlier coverage or a legal cadence reset.

preliminary_notice.name: Owner and construction lender notices
preliminary_notice.description: Lender notice is required within fifteen business days of the later trigger. Remote suppliers also notify owner BEFORE first delivery; retain both candidates.

notice_duties.name: Owner notice before furnishing
notice_duties.description: Give written notice to the owner or person having charge of the property before first furnishing. A later notice has the unpaid-balance limitations in RSA 447:6; preserve the existing late-notice and balance review path.

notice_duties.name: Construction lender notice
notice_duties.description: Provide written notice to the institution providing the construction funds within fifteen business days of the later of first furnishing or the actual jobsite lender posting. Include the name and address of the jobsite. Failure to provide this notice alone does not invalidate the lien (RSA 447:12-b(II)); preserve the bound service and business-day rules.

recurring_notice_checkpoints.name: Written-account check-in
recurring_notice_checkpoints.description: Account check-ins are advisory, not settled RSA 447:8 deadlines. Earlier uncovered or late periods remain unresolved; a later logged account does not cure them, reset a legal cadence or establish legal service.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: Contract grouping or qualifying completion remains unresolved. First furnishing +120 is an early conservative planning checkpoint. The last-furnishing +120 candidate remains informational until its contract and completion are established; first+120 passing does not by itself show that an entire-contract lien has expired. Conservative action date shown; the statutory deadline remains unresolved. Obtain qualified review before this date.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment

The last-furnishing +120 candidate remains informational until its contract and completion are established; first+120 passing does not by itself show that an entire-contract lien has expired. Conservative action date shown; the statutory deadline remains unresolved. Obtain qualified review before this date.

questions.label: Are these qualifying materials for a private real-property improvement?
questions.help: Public projects, bond claims, labor-only claims, inventory/resale and nonqualifying materials require separate review.

questions.label: Is the final furnishing disputed, warranty, corrective, trivial or outside this contract?
questions.help: Is the final furnishing disputed, warranty, corrective, trivial or outside this contract?

questions.label: Is there a waiver, lien bond, disputed property interest, payment/priority issue or identified legal/calendar exception?
questions.help: Identify actual exceptions or known source/version changes; do not assume these facts away.

questions.label: Does this lien claim concern one identified entire contract rather than distinct separate orders?
questions.help: Confirm the contract governing the qualifying materials in this claim. One jobsite, customer, account or group of invoices does not establish one entire contract. If grouping is unresolved, answer unknown. A later replacement, invoice, payment, materials not supplied by you or receivership does not restart a completed contract.

questions.label: Have you actually completed qualifying furnishing for this claim?
questions.help: If this claim is under one identified entire contract, confirm actual qualifying completion of your furnishing under that contract and enter that date. Do not use a planned delivery, project-wide latest delivery, payment, later invoice alone, corrective/trivial replacement or another supplier’s materials to restart a completed contract. If completion or contract linkage is unresolved, answer unknown. With no established entire contract, a known final date remains informational and requires review.

questions.help: Is the qualifying claim at least $15?

questions.help: Is the owner municipal, the hiring party a reseller, or a lower contractor tier unresolved?

questions.label: When was the first qualifying delivery?
questions.help: When was the first qualifying delivery?

questions.label: Is there a construction mortgage requiring lender notice?
questions.help: Is there a construction mortgage requiring lender notice?

questions.label: What is the LATER of first furnishing and the actual lender posting date?
questions.help: What is the LATER of first furnishing and the actual lender posting date?

questions.label: Is the owner notice late or its unpaid-balance effect unresolved?
questions.help: Is the owner notice late or its unpaid-balance effect unresolved?

questions.label: Has the written owner notice actually been given?
questions.help: Enter the actual date the written owner notice under RSA 447:5-7 was given. The planned before-first-delivery target and construction-lender notice are separate and do not establish this act. This optional fact supports written-account review only; no, unknown or omission does not block the existing owner or lender notice calculation. Late-notice and unpaid-balance effects remain subject to the existing review question.

sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. Series09 permits a calculated completion +120 raw baseline only for an explicitly identified entire contract and actual qualifying completion, after existing holds. Unresolved grouping/completion retains review: first +120 is a conservative checkpoint and known final +120 informational; passing the checkpoint alone does not establish expiry. Notice/account clocks, source windows, raw calendar and pending approval remain unchanged. Details and limits remain in the bound note.

October 13 complete Chapter 447 read and the General Court online compilation statement supersede the original access limitation. The website states currency through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026, but identifies Thomson Reuters bound volumes/supplements as the official version. Specific procedure, interpretation and appointment limits remain.
Additional service, recording and amount conditions described below remain mandatory; this calculator is not a notice-sending or lien-filing service.

This is court attachment, not recorder filing. Start well before the target; RSA 511-A procedure remains unread. The October 13 reads include Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), describing an indivisible lien under one entire contract and whole-lien preservation within its historical 90-day period; McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005, describes the 120-day completion clock but decides priority; Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), rejects completed-contract replacement and receivership extensions. The retained first-delivery +120 date is a conservative review target, not a universal statutory expiration. Contract identity/completion, CAP reporter accuracy and current treatment remain qualified.

After the applicable owner notice, provide written accounts as often as once in thirty days. Late notice protects sums then due or that may thereafter become due to the contractor, agent or subcontractor. Unknown mortgage/posting facts require review; do not omit lender notice.

The General Court website states currency through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026. Its displayed LSA links stop at 2023; no separate 2025–2026 bill/LSA search or bound official-edition review is recorded here. Retain the existing targeted election/Thanksgiving evidence and attachment-procedure limits.

recurring_notice_intake.label: Actual owner notice and written accounts
recurring_notice_intake.help: Enter actual written accounts and establish the separate actual owner notice. The latest actual act plus thirty days is an advisory checkpoint only; later accounts do not establish timely earlier coverage or a legal cadence reset.

preliminary_notice.name: Owner and construction lender notices
preliminary_notice.description: Lender notice is required within fifteen business days of the later trigger. Remote suppliers also notify owner BEFORE first delivery; retain both candidates.

notice_duties.name: Owner notice before furnishing
notice_duties.description: Give written notice to the owner or person having charge of the property before first furnishing. A later notice has the unpaid-balance limitations in RSA 447:6; preserve the existing late-notice and balance review path.

notice_duties.name: Construction lender notice
notice_duties.description: Provide written notice to the institution providing the construction funds within fifteen business days of the later of first furnishing or the actual jobsite lender posting. Include the name and address of the jobsite. Failure to provide this notice alone does not invalidate the lien (RSA 447:12-b(II)); preserve the bound service and business-day rules.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: Qualifying completion is not established. First furnishing +120 is an early conservative planning checkpoint, not a universal per-delivery expiration. Resolve the contract and completion; later replacement or materials supplied by someone else cannot automatically restart a completed contract. Conservative action date shown; the statutory deadline remains unresolved. Obtain qualified review before this date.

Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. Series09 permits a calculated completion +120 raw baseline only for an explicitly identified entire contract and actual qualifying completion, after existing holds. Unresolved grouping/completion retains review: first +120 is a conservative checkpoint and known final +120 informational; passing the checkpoint alone does not establish expiry. Notice/account clocks, source windows, raw calendar and pending approval remain unchanged. Details and limits remain in the bound note.

October 13 complete Chapter 447 read and the General Court online compilation statement supersede the original access limitation. The website states currency through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026, but identifies Thomson Reuters bound volumes/supplements as the official version. Specific procedure, interpretation and appointment limits remain.
Additional service, recording and amount conditions described below remain mandatory; this calculator is not a notice-sending or lien-filing service.

This is court attachment, not recorder filing. Start well before the target; RSA 511-A procedure remains unread. The October 13 reads include Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), describing an indivisible lien under one entire contract and whole-lien preservation within its historical 90-day period; McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005, describes the 120-day completion clock but decides priority; Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), rejects completed-contract replacement and receivership extensions. The retained first-delivery +120 date is a conservative review target, not a universal statutory expiration. Contract identity/completion, CAP reporter accuracy and current treatment remain qualified.

After the applicable owner notice, provide written accounts as often as once in thirty days. Late notice protects sums then due or that may thereafter become due to the contractor, agent or subcontractor. Unknown mortgage/posting facts require review; do not omit lender notice.

The General Court website states currency through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026. Its displayed LSA links stop at 2023; no separate 2025–2026 bill/LSA search or bound official-edition review is recorded here. Retain the existing targeted election/Thanksgiving evidence and attachment-procedure limits.

recurring_notice_intake.label: Actual owner notice and written accounts
recurring_notice_intake.help: Enter actual written accounts and establish the separate actual owner notice. The latest actual act plus thirty days is an advisory checkpoint only; later accounts do not establish timely earlier coverage or a legal cadence reset.

preliminary_notice.name: Owner and construction lender notices
preliminary_notice.description: Lender notice is required within fifteen business days of the later trigger. Remote suppliers also notify owner BEFORE first delivery; retain both candidates.

notice_duties.name: Owner notice before furnishing
notice_duties.description: Give written notice to the owner or person having charge of the property before first furnishing. A later notice has the unpaid-balance limitations in RSA 447:6; preserve the existing late-notice and balance review path.

notice_duties.name: Construction lender notice
notice_duties.description: Provide written notice to the institution providing the construction funds within fifteen business days of the later of first furnishing or the actual jobsite lender posting. Include the name and address of the jobsite. Failure to provide this notice alone does not invalidate the lien (RSA 447:12-b(II)); preserve the bound service and business-day rules.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: Qualifying completion is not established. First furnishing +120 is an early conservative planning checkpoint, not a universal per-delivery expiration. Resolve the contract and completion; later replacement or materials supplied by someone else cannot automatically restart a completed contract. Conservative action date shown; the statutory deadline remains unresolved. Obtain qualified review before this date.

questions.label: Are these qualifying materials for a private real-property improvement?
questions.help: Public projects, bond claims, labor-only claims, inventory/resale and nonqualifying materials require separate review.

questions.help: Is the final furnishing disputed, warranty, corrective, trivial or outside this contract?

questions.label: Is there a waiver, lien bond, disputed property interest, payment/priority issue or identified legal/calendar exception?
questions.help: Identify actual exceptions or known source/version changes; do not assume these facts away.

questions.label: Does this lien claim concern one identified entire contract rather than distinct separate orders?
questions.help: Confirm the contract governing the qualifying materials in this claim. One jobsite, customer, account or group of invoices does not establish one entire contract. If grouping is unresolved, answer unknown. A later replacement, invoice, payment, materials not supplied by you or receivership does not restart a completed contract.

questions.label: Have you actually completed qualifying furnishing for this claim?
questions.help: If this claim is under one identified entire contract, confirm actual qualifying completion of your furnishing under that contract and enter that date. Do not use a planned delivery, project-wide latest delivery, payment, later invoice alone, corrective/trivial replacement or another supplier’s materials to restart a completed contract. If completion or contract linkage is unresolved, answer unknown. With no established entire contract, a known final date remains informational and requires review.

questions.help: Enter the actual date the written owner notice under RSA 447:5-7 was given. recurring_notice_intake.label: Actual owner notice and written accounts
recurring_notice_intake.help: Enter actual written accounts and establish the separate actual owner notice. The latest actual act plus thirty days is an advisory checkpoint only; later accounts do not establish timely earlier coverage or a legal cadence reset.

preliminary_notice.name: Owner and construction lender notices
preliminary_notice.description: Lender notice is required within fifteen business days of the later trigger. Remote suppliers also notify owner BEFORE first delivery; retain both candidates.

notice_duties.name: Owner notice before furnishing
notice_duties.description: Give written notice to the owner or person having charge of the property before first furnishing. A later notice has the unpaid-balance limitations in RSA 447:6; preserve the existing late-notice and balance review path.

notice_duties.name: Construction lender notice
notice_duties.description: Provide written notice to the institution providing the construction funds within fifteen business days of the later of first furnishing or the actual jobsite lender posting. Include the name and address of the jobsite. Failure to provide this notice alone does not invalidate the lien (RSA 447:12-b(II)); preserve the bound service and business-day rules.

recurring_notice_checkpoints.name: Written-account check-in
recurring_notice_checkpoints.description: Account check-ins are advisory, not settled RSA 447:8 deadlines. Earlier uncovered or late periods remain unresolved; a later logged account does not cure them, reset a legal cadence or establish legal service.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: Contract grouping or qualifying completion remains unresolved. First furnishing +120 is an early conservative planning checkpoint. The last-furnishing +120 candidate remains informational until its contract and completion are established; first+120 passing does not by itself show that an entire-contract lien has expired. Conservative action date shown; the statutory deadline remains unresolved. Obtain qualified review before this date.

Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. Series09 permits a calculated completion +120 raw baseline only for an explicitly identified entire contract and actual qualifying completion, after existing holds. Unresolved grouping/completion retains review: first +120 is a conservative checkpoint and known final +120 informational; passing the checkpoint alone does not establish expiry. Notice/account clocks, source windows, raw calendar and pending approval remain unchanged. Details and limits remain in the bound note.

This is court attachment, not recorder filing. Start well before the target; RSA 511-A procedure remains unread. The October 13 reads include Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), describing an indivisible lien under one entire contract and whole-lien preservation within its historical 90-day period; McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005, describes the 120-day completion clock but decides priority; Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), rejects completed-contract replacement and receivership extensions. The retained first-delivery +120 date is a conservative review target, not a universal statutory expiration. Contract identity/completion, CAP reporter accuracy and current treatment remain qualified.

After the applicable owner notice, provide written accounts as often as once in thirty days. Late notice protects sums then due or that may thereafter become due to the contractor, agent or subcontractor. Unknown mortgage/posting facts require review; do not omit lender notice.

Retain the existing targeted election/Thanksgiving evidence and attachment-procedure limits.

preliminary_notice.name: Owner and construction lender notices
preliminary_notice.description: Lender notice is required within fifteen business days of the later trigger. Remote suppliers also notify owner BEFORE first delivery; retain both candidates.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: Contract grouping or qualifying completion remains unresolved. First furnishing +120 is an early conservative planning checkpoint. The last-furnishing +120 candidate remains informational until its contract and completion are established; first+120 passing does not by itself show that an entire-contract lien has expired. Conservative action date shown; the statutory deadline remains unresolved. Obtain qualified review before this date.

questions.help: Identify actual exceptions or known source/version changes; do not assume these facts away.

questions.label: Does this lien claim concern one identified entire contract rather than distinct separate orders?
questions.help: Confirm the contract governing the qualifying materials in this claim. One jobsite, customer, account or group of invoices does not establish one entire contract. If grouping is unresolved, answer unknown. A later replacement, invoice, payment, materials not supplied by you or receivership does not restart a completed contract.

questions.label: Have you actually completed qualifying furnishing for this claim?
questions.help: If this claim is under one identified entire contract, confirm actual qualifying completion of your furnishing under that contract and enter that date. Do not use a planned delivery, project-wide latest delivery, payment, later invoice alone, corrective/trivial replacement or another supplier’s materials to restart a completed contract. If completion or contract linkage is unresolved, answer unknown. With no established entire contract, a known final date remains informational and requires review.

sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. Series09 permits a calculated completion +120 raw baseline only for an explicitly identified entire contract and actual qualifying completion, after existing holds. Unresolved grouping/completion retains review: first +120 is a conservative checkpoint and known final +120 informational; passing the checkpoint alone does not establish expiry. Notice/account clocks, source windows, raw calendar and pending approval remain unchanged. Details and limits remain in the bound note.

This is court attachment, not recorder filing. Start well before the target; RSA 511-A procedure remains unread. The October 13 reads include Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), describing an indivisible lien under one entire contract and whole-lien preservation within its historical 90-day period; McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005, describes the 120-day completion clock but decides priority; Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), rejects completed-contract replacement and receivership extensions. The retained first-delivery +120 date is a conservative review target, not a universal statutory expiration. Contract identity/completion, CAP reporter accuracy and current treatment remain qualified.

After the applicable owner notice, provide written accounts as often as once in thirty days. Late notice protects sums then due or that may thereafter become due to the contractor, agent or subcontractor. Unknown mortgage/posting facts require review; do not omit lender notice.

lien_filing.description: Qualifying completion is not established. First furnishing +120 is an early conservative planning checkpoint, not a universal per-delivery expiration. Resolve the contract and completion; later replacement or materials supplied by someone else cannot automatically restart a completed contract. Conservative action date shown; the statutory deadline remains unresolved. Obtain qualified review before this date.

recurring_notice_intake.label: Actual owner notice and written accounts

notice_duties.name: Owner notice before furnishing

notice_duties.name: Construction lender notice
notice_duties.description: Provide written notice to the institution providing the construction funds within fifteen business days of the later of first furnishing or the actual jobsite lender posting. Include the name and address of the jobsite. Failure to provide this notice alone does not invalidate the lien (RSA 447:12-b(II)); preserve the bound service and business-day rules.

sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. Series09 permits a calculated completion +120 raw baseline only for an explicitly identified entire contract and actual qualifying completion, after existing holds. Unresolved grouping/completion retains review: first +120 is a conservative checkpoint and known final +120 informational; passing the checkpoint alone does not establish expiry. Notice/account clocks, source windows, raw calendar and pending approval remain unchanged. Details and limits remain in the bound note.

recurring_notice_intake.label: Actual owner notice and written accounts
recurring_notice_intake.help: Enter actual written accounts and establish the separate actual owner notice. The latest actual act plus thirty days is an advisory checkpoint only; later accounts do not establish timely earlier coverage or a legal cadence reset.

preliminary_notice.name: Owner and construction lender notices
preliminary_notice.description: Lender notice is required within fifteen business days of the later trigger. Remote suppliers also notify owner BEFORE first delivery; retain both candidates.

notice_duties.name: Owner notice before furnishing
notice_duties.description: Give written notice to the owner or person having charge of the property before first furnishing. A later notice has the unpaid-balance limitations in RSA 447:6; preserve the existing late-notice and balance review path.

notice_duties.name: Construction lender notice
notice_duties.description: Provide written notice to the institution providing the construction funds within fifteen business days of the later of first furnishing or the actual jobsite lender posting. Include the name and address of the jobsite. Failure to provide this notice alone does not invalidate the lien (RSA 447:12-b(II)); preserve the bound service and business-day rules.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: Contract grouping or qualifying completion remains unresolved. First furnishing +120 is an early conservative planning checkpoint. The last-furnishing +120 candidate remains informational until its contract and completion are established; first+120 passing does not by itself show that an entire-contract lien has expired. Conservative action date shown; the statutory deadline remains unresolved. Obtain qualified review before this date.

preliminary_notice.description: Lender notice is required within fifteen business days of the later trigger. Remote suppliers also notify owner BEFORE first delivery; retain both candidates.

notice_duties.name: Owner notice before furnishing
notice_duties.description: Give written notice to the owner or person having charge of the property before first furnishing. A later notice has the unpaid-balance limitations in RSA 447:6; preserve the existing late-notice and balance review path.

notice_duties.name: Construction lender notice
notice_duties.description: Provide written notice to the institution providing the construction funds within fifteen business days of the later of first furnishing or the actual jobsite lender posting. Include the name and address of the jobsite. Failure to provide this notice alone does not invalidate the lien (RSA 447:12-b(II)); preserve the bound service and business-day rules.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: Qualifying completion is not established. First furnishing +120 is an early conservative planning checkpoint, not a universal per-delivery expiration. Resolve the contract and completion; later replacement or materials supplied by someone else cannot automatically restart a completed contract. Conservative action date shown; the statutory deadline remains unresolved. Obtain qualified review before this date.

Series09 permits a calculated completion +120 raw baseline only for an explicitly identified entire contract and actual qualifying completion, after existing holds. Notice/account clocks, source windows, raw calendar and pending approval remain unchanged. Details and limits remain in the bound note.

Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. Series09 permits a calculated completion +120 raw baseline only for an explicitly identified entire contract and actual qualifying completion, after existing holds. Unresolved grouping/completion retains review: first +120 is a conservative checkpoint and known final +120 informational; passing the checkpoint alone does not establish expiry. Notice/account clocks, source windows, raw calendar and pending approval remain unchanged. Details and limits remain in the bound note.

recurring_notice_intake.label: Actual owner notice and written accounts
recurring_notice_intake.help: Enter actual written accounts and establish the separate actual owner notice. The latest actual act plus thirty days is an advisory checkpoint only; later accounts do not establish timely earlier coverage or a legal cadence reset.

preliminary_notice.name: Owner and construction lender notices
preliminary_notice.description: Lender notice is required within fifteen business days of the later trigger. Remote suppliers also notify owner BEFORE first delivery; retain both candidates.

notice_duties.name: Owner notice before furnishing
notice_duties.description: Give written notice to the owner or person having charge of the property before first furnishing. A later notice has the unpaid-balance limitations in RSA 447:6; preserve the existing late-notice and balance review path.

notice_duties.name: Construction lender notice
notice_duties.description: Provide written notice to the institution providing the construction funds within fifteen business days of the later of first furnishing or the actual jobsite lender posting. Include the name and address of the jobsite. Failure to provide this notice alone does not invalidate the lien (RSA 447:12-b(II)); preserve the bound service and business-day rules.

recurring_notice_checkpoints.name: Written-account check-in
recurring_notice_checkpoints.description: Account check-ins are advisory, not settled RSA 447:8 deadlines. Earlier uncovered or late periods remain unresolved; a later logged account does not cure them, reset a legal cadence or establish legal service.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: For an established entire contract with actual qualifying furnishing completed, secure the lien by court attachment within the calculated 120-day baseline. This is not a determination of notice coverage, amount, priority or attachment procedure; start court work well before this date.

questions.label: Does this lien claim concern one identified entire contract rather than distinct separate orders?

Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. Series09 permits a calculated completion +120 raw baseline only for an explicitly identified entire contract and actual qualifying completion, after existing holds. Unresolved grouping/completion retains review: first +120 is a conservative checkpoint and known final +120 informational; passing the checkpoint alone does not establish expiry. Notice/account clocks, source windows, raw calendar and pending approval remain unchanged. Details and limits remain in the bound note.

recurring_notice_intake.label: Actual owner notice and written accounts
recurring_notice_intake.help: Enter actual written accounts and establish the separate actual owner notice. The latest actual act plus thirty days is an advisory checkpoint only; later accounts do not establish timely earlier coverage or a legal cadence reset.

preliminary_notice.name: Owner and construction lender notices
preliminary_notice.description: Lender notice is required within fifteen business days of the later trigger. Remote suppliers also notify owner BEFORE first delivery; retain both candidates.

notice_duties.name: Owner notice before furnishing
notice_duties.description: Give written notice to the owner or person having charge of the property before first furnishing. A later notice has the unpaid-balance limitations in RSA 447:6; preserve the existing late-notice and balance review path.

notice_duties.name: Construction lender notice
notice_duties.description: Provide written notice to the institution providing the construction funds within fifteen business days of the later of first furnishing or the actual jobsite lender posting. Include the name and address of the jobsite. Failure to provide this notice alone does not invalidate the lien (RSA 447:12-b(II)); preserve the bound service and business-day rules.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: Qualifying completion is not established. First furnishing +120 is an early conservative planning checkpoint, not a universal per-delivery expiration. Resolve the contract and completion; later replacement or materials supplied by someone else cannot automatically restart a completed contract. Conservative action date shown; the statutory deadline remains unresolved. Obtain qualified review before this date.

sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. Series09 permits a calculated completion +120 raw baseline only for an explicitly identified entire contract and actual qualifying completion, after existing holds. Unresolved grouping/completion retains review: first +120 is a conservative checkpoint and known final +120 informational; passing the checkpoint alone does not establish expiry. Notice/account clocks, source windows, raw calendar and pending approval remain unchanged. Details and limits remain in the bound note.

recurring_notice_intake.label: Actual owner notice and written accounts
recurring_notice_intake.help: Enter actual written accounts and establish the separate actual owner notice. The latest actual act plus thirty days is an advisory checkpoint only; later accounts do not establish timely earlier coverage or a legal cadence reset.

preliminary_notice.name: Owner and construction lender notices
preliminary_notice.description: Lender notice is required within fifteen business days of the later trigger. Remote suppliers also notify owner BEFORE first delivery; retain both candidates.

notice_duties.name: Owner notice before furnishing
notice_duties.description: Give written notice to the owner or person having charge of the property before first furnishing. A later notice has the unpaid-balance limitations in RSA 447:6; preserve the existing late-notice and balance review path.

notice_duties.name: Construction lender notice
notice_duties.description: Provide written notice to the institution providing the construction funds within fifteen business days of the later of first furnishing or the actual jobsite lender posting. Include the name and address of the jobsite. Failure to provide this notice alone does not invalidate the lien (RSA 447:12-b(II)); preserve the bound service and business-day rules.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: Qualifying completion is not established. First furnishing +120 is an early conservative planning checkpoint, not a universal per-delivery expiration. Resolve the contract and completion; later replacement or materials supplied by someone else cannot automatically restart a completed contract. Conservative action date shown; the statutory deadline remains unresolved. Obtain qualified review before this date.

Include the name and address of the jobsite. Failure to provide this notice alone does not invalidate the lien (RSA 447:12-b(II)); preserve the bound service and business-day rules.

recurring_notice_checkpoints.name: Written-account check-in
recurring_notice_checkpoints.description: Account check-ins are advisory, not settled RSA 447:8 deadlines. Earlier uncovered or late periods remain unresolved; a later logged account does not cure them, reset a legal cadence or establish legal service.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: For an established entire contract with actual qualifying furnishing completed, secure the lien by court attachment within the calculated 120-day baseline. This is not a determination of notice coverage, amount, priority or attachment procedure; start court work well before this date.

sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. Series09 permits a calculated completion +120 raw baseline only for an explicitly identified entire contract and actual qualifying completion, after existing holds. Unresolved grouping/completion retains review: first +120 is a conservative checkpoint and known final +120 informational; passing the checkpoint alone does not establish expiry. Notice/account clocks, source windows, raw calendar and pending approval remain unchanged. Details and limits remain in the bound note.

The retained first-delivery +120 date is a conservative review target, not a universal statutory expiration. Contract identity/completion, CAP reporter accuracy and current treatment remain qualified.

After the applicable owner notice, provide written accounts as often as once in thirty days. Late notice protects sums then due or that may thereafter become due to the contractor, agent or subcontractor. Unknown mortgage/posting facts require review; do not omit lender notice.

questions.help: Is the final furnishing disputed, warranty, corrective, trivial or outside this contract?

questions.label: Is there a waiver, lien bond, disputed property interest, payment/priority issue or identified legal/calendar exception?
questions.help: Identify actual exceptions or known source/version changes; do not assume these facts away.

questions.label: Does this lien claim concern one identified entire contract rather than distinct separate orders?
questions.help: Confirm the contract governing the qualifying materials in this claim. One jobsite, customer, account or group of invoices does not establish one entire contract. If grouping is unresolved, answer unknown. A later replacement, invoice, payment, materials not supplied by you or receivership does not restart a completed contract.

questions.label: Have you actually completed qualifying furnishing for this claim?
questions.help: If this claim is under one identified entire contract, confirm actual qualifying completion of your furnishing under that contract and enter that date. Do not use a planned delivery, project-wide latest delivery, payment, later invoice alone, corrective/trivial replacement or another supplier’s materials to restart a completed contract. If completion or contract linkage is unresolved, answer unknown. With no established entire contract, a known final date remains informational and requires review.

sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. Series09 permits a calculated completion +120 raw baseline only for an explicitly identified entire contract and actual qualifying completion, after existing holds. Unresolved grouping/completion retains review: first +120 is a conservative checkpoint and known final +120 informational; passing the checkpoint alone does not establish expiry. Notice/account clocks, source windows, raw calendar and pending approval remain unchanged. Details and limits remain in the bound note.

Specific procedure, interpretation and appointment limits remain.
Additional service, recording and amount conditions described below remain mandatory; this calculator is not a notice-sending or lien-filing service.

This is court attachment, not recorder filing. Start well before the target; RSA 511-A procedure remains unread. The October 13 reads include Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), describing an indivisible lien under one entire contract and whole-lien preservation within its historical 90-day period; McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005, describes the 120-day completion clock but decides priority; Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), rejects completed-contract replacement and receivership extensions. The retained first-delivery +120 date is a conservative review target, not a universal statutory expiration. Contract identity/completion, CAP reporter accuracy and current treatment remain qualified.

After the applicable owner notice, provide written accounts as often as once in thirty days. Late notice protects sums then due or that may thereafter become due to the contractor, agent or subcontractor. Unknown mortgage/posting facts require review; do not omit lender notice.

The General Court website states currency through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026. Its displayed LSA links stop at 2023; no separate 2025–2026 bill/LSA search or bound official-edition review is recorded here. Retain the existing targeted election/Thanksgiving evidence and attachment-procedure limits.

recurring_notice_intake.label: Actual owner notice and written accounts
recurring_notice_intake.help: Enter actual written accounts and establish the separate actual owner notice. The latest actual act plus thirty days is an advisory checkpoint only; later accounts do not establish timely earlier coverage or a legal cadence reset.

preliminary_notice.name: Owner and construction lender notices
preliminary_notice.description: Lender notice is required within fifteen business days of the later trigger. Remote suppliers also notify owner BEFORE first delivery; retain both candidates.

notice_duties.name: Owner notice before furnishing
notice_duties.description: Give written notice to the owner or person having charge of the property before first furnishing. A later notice has the unpaid-balance limitations in RSA 447:6; preserve the existing late-notice and balance review path.

notice_duties.name: Construction lender notice
notice_duties.description: Provide written notice to the institution providing the construction funds within fifteen business days of the later of first furnishing or the actual jobsite lender posting. Include the name and address of the jobsite. Failure to provide this notice alone does not invalidate the lien (RSA 447:12-b(II)); preserve the bound service and business-day rules.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: Contract grouping or qualifying completion remains unresolved. First furnishing +120 is an early conservative planning checkpoint. The last-furnishing +120 candidate remains informational until its contract and completion are established; first+120 passing does not by itself show that an entire-contract lien has expired. Conservative action date shown; the statutory deadline remains unresolved. Obtain qualified review before this date.

questions.label: Are these qualifying materials for a private real-property improvement?
questions.help: Public projects, bond claims, labor-only claims, inventory/resale and nonqualifying materials require separate review.

questions.label: Is the final furnishing disputed, warranty, corrective, trivial or outside this contract?
questions.help: Is the final furnishing disputed, warranty, corrective, trivial or outside this contract?

questions.label: Is there a waiver, lien bond, disputed property interest, payment/priority issue or identified legal/calendar exception?
questions.help: Identify actual exceptions or known source/version changes; do not assume these facts away.

questions.label: Does this lien claim concern one identified entire contract rather than distinct separate orders?
questions.help: Confirm the contract governing the qualifying materials in this claim. One jobsite, customer, account or group of invoices does not establish one entire contract. If grouping is unresolved, answer unknown. A later replacement, invoice, payment, materials not supplied by you or receivership does not restart a completed contract.

questions.label: Have you actually completed qualifying furnishing for this claim?
questions.help: If this claim is under one identified entire contract, confirm actual qualifying completion of your furnishing under that contract and enter that date. Do not use a planned delivery, project-wide latest delivery, payment, later invoice alone, corrective/trivial replacement or another supplier’s materials to restart a completed contract. If completion or contract linkage is unresolved, answer unknown. With no established entire contract, a known final date remains informational and requires review.

questions.label: Is the qualifying claim at least $15?
questions.help: Is the qualifying claim at least $15?

questions.label: Is the owner municipal, the hiring party a reseller, or a lower contractor tier unresolved?
questions.help: Is the owner municipal, the hiring party a reseller, or a lower contractor tier unresolved?

questions.label: When was the first qualifying delivery?
questions.help: When was the first qualifying delivery?

questions.label: Is there a construction mortgage requiring lender notice?
questions.help: Is there a construction mortgage requiring lender notice?

questions.label: What is the LATER of first furnishing and the actual lender posting date?
questions.help: What is the LATER of first furnishing and the actual lender posting date?

questions.label: Is the owner notice late or its unpaid-balance effect unresolved?
questions.help: Is the owner notice late or its unpaid-balance effect unresolved?

questions.label: Has the written owner notice actually been given?
questions.help: Enter the actual date the written owner notice under RSA 447:5-7 was given. The planned before-first-delivery target and construction-lender notice are separate and do not establish this act. This optional fact supports written-account review only; no, unknown or omission does not block the existing owner or lender notice calculation. Late-notice and unpaid-balance effects remain subject to the existing review question.

recurring_notice_intake.label: Actual owner notice and written accounts
recurring_notice_intake.help: Enter actual written accounts and establish the separate actual owner notice. The latest actual act plus thirty days is an advisory checkpoint only; later accounts do not establish timely earlier coverage or a legal cadence reset.

preliminary_notice.name: Owner and construction lender notices
preliminary_notice.description: Give written owner notice before first delivery.

notice_duties.name: Owner notice before furnishing
notice_duties.description: Give written notice to the owner or person having charge of the property before first furnishing. A later notice has the unpaid-balance limitations in RSA 447:6; preserve the existing late-notice and balance review path.

recurring_notice_checkpoints.name: Written-account check-in
recurring_notice_checkpoints.description: Account check-ins are advisory, not settled RSA 447:8 deadlines. Earlier uncovered or late periods remain unresolved; a later logged account does not cure them, reset a legal cadence or establish legal service.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: For an established entire contract with actual qualifying furnishing completed, secure the lien by court attachment within the calculated 120-day baseline. This is not a determination of notice coverage, amount, priority or attachment procedure; start court work well before this date.
